findings.en_sentence: The distribution of gastroliths found with a D. hallorum fossil suggests these animals may have had a digestive system similar to modern birds, with a crop and gizzard.
findings.problem: Presents the bird-like crop/gizzard (gastric mill) inference from Seismosaurus gastroliths without caveat; Wings & Sander (2007) showed sauropod gastroliths do not support an avian-style gastric mill, and the association of the D. hallorum stones has been questioned.
findings.correct: Gillette suggested in the 1990s that gastroliths found with D. hallorum pointed to a bird-like gizzard, but later studies found no evidence for a gastric mill in sauropods.
findings.checked_in: F124 (eswiki), knowledge (Wings & Sander 2007, Proc. R. Soc. B)

findings.en_sentence: The distribution of gastroliths found with a D. hallorum fossil suggests these animals may have had a digestive system similar to modern birds, with a crop and gizzard.
findings.problem: D. hallorum is cited as if known, but the page never introduces this species (only D. carnegii and D. longus appear).
findings.correct: Introduce it, e.g. 'a fossil of the giant species D. hallorum (originally named Seismosaurus)'.

findings.en_sentence: The distribution of gastroliths found with a D. hallorum fossil suggests these animals may have had a digestive system similar to modern birds, with a crop and gizzard.
findings.problem: The gastrolith sentence exists in English but has no counterpart in the Spanish paleobiology section.
findings.correct: Add the (corrected) sentence to the Spanish text or drop it from both.

findings.en_sentence: Since the 1970s, the general consensus considers sauropods as firmly terrestrial animals, browsing among trees, ferns, and shrubs.
findings.problem: The sentence on the post-1970s consensus of sauropods as terrestrial browsers exists in English but is missing from the Spanish time_and_habitat section.
findings.correct: Add 'Desde la década de 1970, el consenso considera a los saurópodos animales plenamente terrestres que ramoneaban entre árboles, helechos y arbustos.'

findings.en_sentence: Diplodocus is the type genus and namesake of the family Diplodocidae.
findings.es_sentence: El Diplodocus es el género tipo y el nombre de la familia Diplodocidae.
findings.problem: 'es ... el nombre de la familia Diplodocidae' says the genus IS the family's name; the source says it gives its name to the family.
findings.correct: El Diplodocus es el género tipo de la familia Diplodocidae, a la que da nombre.

findings.en_sentence: The animal possessed highly unusual teeth with long, slender crowns that were elliptical in cross-section and ended in a blunt, triangular point.
findings.es_sentence: El animal poseía dientes altamente inusuales con coronas largas y delgadas, elípticas en sección transversal y terminadas en un punto triangular y obtuso.
findings.problem: 'terminadas en un punto triangular' uses 'punto' (point/dot) for the tooth apex; the correct word is 'punta'. 'altamente inusuales' is also a calque of 'highly unusual'.
findings.correct: ...dientes muy inusuales, con coronas largas y delgadas, de sección elíptica y terminadas en una punta triangular roma.

findings.en_sentence: Sauropod footprints found in the 1930s disproved the theory that Diplodocus had a sprawling, lizard-like gait.
findings.es_sentence: Las huellas de saurópodos encontradas en los años 1930 desmintieron la teoría de que el Diplodocus tenía una marcha extendida, similar a la de los lagartos.
findings.problem: 'marcha extendida' does not convey 'sprawling gait' (limbs splayed out to the sides).
findings.correct: ...la teoría de que el Diplodocus caminaba con las patas abiertas hacia los lados, como los lagartos (postura reptante).

findings.en_sentence: These massive reptiles held their bodies horizontally, with forelimbs noticeably shorter than their powerful hind legs.
findings.es_sentence: Estos reptiles masivos mantenían el cuerpo horizontal, con las extremidades anteriores notablemente más cortas que las poderosas patas traseras.
findings.problem: 'reptiles masivos' is a calque of 'massive'; in Spanish 'masivo' means multitudinous/large-scale.
findings.correct: Estos enormes reptiles mantenían el cuerpo horizontal...

findings.en_sentence: This giant could rear up onto its hind legs and tail to form a stable three-point stance, potentially reaching food 11 meters high.
findings.es_sentence: Este gigante podía erguirse sobre las patas traseras y la cola para formar una postura estable de tres puntos, alcanzando potencialmente comida a 11 metros de altura.
findings.problem: 'postura estable de tres puntos' and 'alcanzando potencialmente comida' are literal calques; the usual term is 'postura trípode'.
findings.correct: ...para adoptar una postura trípode estable, con la que quizá alcanzaba alimento a 11 metros de altura.

findings.en_sentence: Up to five replacement teeth were developing within each tooth socket at any given time.
findings.es_sentence: Hasta cinco dientes de reemplazo se desarrollaban dentro de cada alveolo dental en cualquier momento dado.
findings.problem: 'en cualquier momento dado' calques 'at any given time'.
findings.correct: En cada alveolo se desarrollaban a la vez hasta cinco dientes de reemplazo.

findings.en_sentence: Remarkably, the tail alone accounted for about 55 percent of the animal's total body length.
findings.es_sentence: Sorprendentemente, la cola sola representaba aproximadamente el 55 % de la longitud total del animal.
findings.problem: 'la cola sola' is awkward/ambiguous ('the lonely tail'); should be 'por sí sola' or 'solo la cola'.
findings.correct: Sorprendentemente, solo la cola representaba aproximadamente el 55 % de la longitud total del animal.
